.²1 Fragrance, odour, sweet scent; {#sOraByaM Buvanatraye'pi viditam#}
 <ls>Bv. 1. 38</ls>; {#punAnA sOraByEH#} <ls>G. L. 43</ls>; <ls>R. 5. 69</ls>.

.²3 Good character, reputation, glory, fame. [<ls>Dr. Kṣitīśachandra Chatterjee</ls>
 writes in Mañjūṣā, “Like {#cApala#} and {#cApalya#}, both {#sOraBa#}
 and {#sOraBya#} are found in Sanskrit, but Pāṇini has made provision
 for both {#cApala#} and {#cApalya#} by including the word {#capala#} both
 in the {#yuvAdi#} group and in the {#brAhmaRAdi#} group. {#suraBi#} is
 included in neither of these groups but comes under the purview of the
 rule {#igantAcca laGupUrvAt#} and so the only form sanctioned by Pāṇini
 is {#sOraBa#}. It would appear that {#sOraBya#} came into use later on
 after the analogy of {#sOganDya#}.]”
